tema: Future in the Past — Was Going To, Would, Was About To, Was To

cast_dialogue.linea: Stories look backwards at futures that were still asleep, heroes. 'He was about to sign when...' — the grammar of destiny.
I was going to study engineering, but a trip to the mountains changed everything.
You were about to enrol when you found your grandfather's camera, right? That camera was to change your life.
The exhibition that would make him famous was still ten years away. Nobody knew it yet.
He was on the verge of signing the papers when he chose his dream, mis héroes. The bravest futures start as a 'no' to the expected path.

banco_oraciones.oracion: He was going to study engineering.
He was about to enrol when he found the camera.
That day, he was to become a photographer.
The exhibition would make him famous ten years later.
He wasn't going to study photography.
Nobody knew what was to come.
He wasn't on the verge of giving up.
Was he going to study engineering?
What was he about to do when he found the camera?
Was he going to sign? Yes, he was about to.
Did anyone know? No, nobody did.
Was that his destiny? Yes, it was to be.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Looking at the future FROM the past: was/were going to (past plan), would (the future seen from then), was about to + verb (imminent), was to + verb (formal destiny, often for events that really happened later), on the verge of + -ing (at the edge).

ejercicios.pregunta: Tell a turning point in your life using 'was going to' and 'was about to'.
ejercicios.respuesta: I was going to study law, but I changed my mind. I was about to enrol when I discovered my passion for design.

guion: Sofía: Ben, is it true you almost studied engineering?
Ben: Yes! I was going to study it at university. I had everything ready.
Ben: I was about to enrol when I found my grandfather's old camera in the attic.
Sofía: Wow. And that changed everything?
Ben: Completely. That camera was to become my whole life.
Sofía: And the exhibition that would make you famous was still ten years away...
Ben: Exactly. I was on the verge of signing the papers when I chose photography instead.
